newsitem.title: USA: J.C. Penney takes the US corp bond spotlight.
newsitem.headline: J.C. Penney takes the US corp bond spotlight.

text.p: J.C. Penney's multi-tranche debt offering has taken the corporate bond primary spotlight yet again, as growing demand for the deal led the underwriter to increase the offering to $2.3 billion, dealers said.
As investors scramble to get a piece of the offering, other issuers, contemplating whether or not to move on with their own financing, are keeping a watchful eye on the deal.
J.C. Penney's deal, initially set as a $2.0 billion five-part debt offering, was restructured to include an additional $300 million three-year tranche, dealer said.
Dealers said if the deal continues to gain momentum the size of the offering may be increased yet again.
"Talk in the market is that the deal may go higher than the $2.3 billion," said another dealer. "We're hearing that the five-year tranche may be upped in size as well."
The six-part $2.3 billion debt offering, which will be launched later this morning, includes the following tranches, dealers said.
-$300 million of a three-year issue with price talk seen betwwen 40-45 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
-$600 million of a five-year issue with price talk seen between +45-50 basis points over Treasuries.
-$400 million of a 10-year issue with price talk seen at +70 basis points over Treasuries.
-$300 million in 20-year debt with price talk seen at +85 basis points over Treasuries.
-$350 million of a 30-year bond, callable after 10 years, with price talk seen at +120 basis points area.
-$350 million of a 40-year bonds, putable in eight years, is seen in the mid-40's basis points range.
Credit Suisse First Boston is expected to serve as lead underwriter for the offering.
Meanwhile players are expecting J.C. Penney's deal will set the tone in the market for other issuers who are on the sidelines contemplating their own offerings.

A recent rise in U.S. interest rates had forced many issuers to head for the sidelines as they faced higher borrowing cost following a 1/4 point hike by the U.S. Federal Reserve Board in the overnight lending rate.

In addition, Hilton Hotels is expectd to tap the primary market with a $300 million 10-year note deal. The offering carries a coupon reset provision in the event of a downgrade to a speculative grade level, sources said.
The reset provision consist of the following breakdown, according to market sources.
Moody's /S&P Spread
Ba1 /BB-plus 175 basis points over Treasuries
Ba2 /BB 210 basis points over Treasuries
Ba3 /BB-minus 250 basis points over Treasuries
B1 /B-plus or below 325 basis points over Treasuries
The Baa1/BBB-plus rated Hilton offering is expected to be underwritten by Merrill Lynch & Co.
In the high-yield sector, Syratech Corp is expected to issue $155 million in 10-year senior notes via Nationsbanc Capital Markets, sources said.

Other names include Anchor Glass Container's $150 million in 144A first mortgage notes due 2005, Consumer International's $170 million 144A notes due 2005 and Greyhound Lines' $150 million 144A notes due 2007, sources said.
Sun World International is also expected to price $115 million in 144A mortgage notes due 2004.
In the government market, the benchmark U.S. 30-year bond was unchanged Wednesday morning at 94-4/32 to yield 7.10 percent.
